chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: Four-tune sessions, flip-side hits and morning recording
summary: A session was four numbers, the fourth often a book tune; the throwaway back-up sometimes became the hit. Morning sessions, especially Mondays after Sunday off, were best.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Sure. When -- did you often go into record new tunes especially, or simply recorded things that you had in the book and you --
Well, there was some of both. For
instance, like I think -- if I can remember correctly -- a session constituted four numbers.
That's what it seems to be according to --

Yeah. Four numbers, and sometimes that fourth number -- you wouldn't know what it was gonna be, maybe they might change it then, see. They'd have probably three numbers set, and the fourth number -- it would be some hidden thing in the books there, and a funny thing about it, sometimes you would record a tune that's supposed to be the hit on one side, and just put a back up on the other, and it turned out sometime that the back up tune was the hit. It was a funny thing, you know. I wish I had the little book here. I could, I guess -- It's pretty obvious though. I explained it like it would be. But sometimes a guy would come up and say, this is our hit tune. This is gonna be a hit, one of those things. What are you gonna back it up with? Oh, play anything. Put anything on the back. The anything on the back turned out to be the swinger. That was funny. But That's music.
Did the sessions -- what time of day did they normally occur?
We always did a lot of things in the morning. They figure that, well, either the musician has been out all night, and regardless of the fact if he's tired, he's still gonna play.
Yeah. He's gonna be pretty loose and ready to go.

Later on in the evening, they always find out they're lazy, you know, and want to go to bed or get sleepy. Their playing isn't as clean as it would ordinarily be. If I remember correctly, I found out that the morning sessions were mostly the best. But I'll tell you another thing that helped though, the fact that a lot of the sessions were in the mornings -- like on Monday morning after your day off on Sunday. You've had a little time, you know. (unintelligible)
I'd hate to have heard them on a Saturday or Sunday morning.
Or a big Saturday night, huh?
Did the -- I lost track of what I was going to say --
Yeah. It was something about that. Can't think of it right now.
Well, maybe it'll come to you.
